question: What Does Elementor Pro Add Over the Free Version?
metaDescription: Theme Builder, popups, forms, dynamic content, more widgets and third-party integrations — the free version covers basic page-building only.
shortAnswer: The free version of Elementor covers solid page-building basics — a good widget set, responsive editing, and the core drag-and-drop canvas. Elementor Pro adds the Theme Builder (custom headers, footers, archive and single templates), the Popup Builder, the Form widget, dynamic content tags pulling from custom fields, many additional widgets, and integrations with email marketing and CRM tools that the free version doesn't include.

bodyHtml:
What's Actually in Each Tier

Free Elementor is genuinely usable for building individual pages with a solid range of layout and content widgets, but it stops at the page level — it can't touch the header, footer, or template files that wrap around your content, and it lacks a native way to collect form submissions or trigger popups. Elementor Pro extends the same familiar editor across the entire site through its Theme Builder, and adds the dedicated tools (forms, popups, dynamic tags) most real sites eventually need.

Key Pro-Only Features

  • Theme Builder, letting you design custom headers, footers, single post/product templates, and archive templates visually, replacing what would otherwise require custom theme code.
  • Popup Builder, for exit-intent offers, newsletter signups, and other triggered overlays, with its own targeting and display conditions.
  • The Form widget, collecting submissions and routing them to email, a database, or third-party integrations without a separate forms plugin.
  • Dynamic Tags, pulling content from custom fields, post meta, or WooCommerce product data directly into a design rather than hardcoding it.
  • Additional widgets (price tables, testimonials carousels, advanced sliders, and more) beyond the free widget set.

Deciding Whether You Need Pro

  1. Stick with free if you only need to design individual page content and already have separate forms/popup solutions.
  2. Upgrade to Pro once you need custom headers/footers, forms, popups, or dynamic content pulled from custom fields.
  3. Check for widget or plugin overlap before upgrading, since Pro may replace other plugins you're currently paying for separately.

Need help deciding what Elementor setup actually fits your site? See Elementor customization.
